landingIntro: A little curiosity on your commute or during a break. Learn at your own pace with KAQ, from AWS basics to AWS certification learning.
freeStudyAnswer: Practice questions, mock exams, and reviewing incorrect answers are free. Creating an account is free too.
guestStudyQuestion: Can I study without an account?
guestStudyAnswer: You can practice questions, take mock exams, and review incorrect answers without signing up. If you allow storage on this device, guest study records stay on this device.
accountTradeoffsQuestion: Are there any downsides to creating an account?
accountTradeoffsAnswer: You need to sign in through an external service. We use your sign-in provider’s user ID and basic profile information you agree to share, such as your email address, for authentication. Study records saved to a signed-in KAQ account sync across devices. You can view your learning history in the dashboard.
mockFormatQuestion: Can I choose the number of questions and the time limit for a mock exam?
mockFormatAnswer: Choose Short, Medium, Full, or Custom. You can see the question count and time limit before starting. Custom lets you set the number of questions.
answerExplanationsQuestion: Can I see explanations after answering?
answerExplanationsAnswer: After answering, you can see why each option is correct or incorrect. You can also open the relevant official AWS documentation.
commuteStudyQuestion: Can I study during a short commute?
commuteStudyAnswer: Answer a single question on your phone while you wait for the train or bus. Read the explanation as soon as you answer. If you have a little more time, try a short mock exam.
studyPathsIntro: Start with the basics or practice with certification questions and mock exams.

guideClfScope: Checks understanding of the value of AWS Cloud, the shared responsibility model, the roles of key services, pricing, and support.
guideClfWhy: Focuses on basic terminology and choosing services for different uses.
guideClfAudience: People new to AWS, or those in sales and planning who want a shared understanding of cloud fundamentals with development teams.
guideAifScope: Covers AI, machine learning, and generative AI fundamentals, foundation model uses, responsible AI, and data governance.
guideAifWhy: Explaining use cases and risks matters more than implementing models.
guideAifAudience: People involved in AI-based planning or process improvement, and those beginning to learn AI development.
guideSaaScope: Covers designing secure, highly available AWS architectures that meet performance and cost requirements.
guideSaaWhy: You choose among similar architectures to meet constraints such as availability, connectivity paths, and operational effort.
guideSaaAudience: Infrastructure engineers, SREs, and application developers who want to learn AWS architecture systematically.
guideDvaScope: Covers application development on AWS, AI-assisted development, authentication and permissions, testing, deployment, and troubleshooting.
guideDvaWhy: Tests implementation behavior, such as Lambda retries and DynamoDB conditional updates.
guideDvaAudience: Developers building backends or serverless applications with AWS managed services.
guideSoaScope: Covers monitoring, reliability, incident response, networking, and operational automation in AWS environments.
guideSoaWhy: You isolate causes from symptoms and choose recovery and improvement methods that fit operational constraints.
guideSoaAudience: Cloud operators and SREs who want a systematic approach to monitoring and incident response.
guideDeaScope: Covers data ingestion, transformation, storage, pipeline operations, and access management.
guideDeaWhy: Requires understanding how latency, reruns, cost, and access control differ across processing approaches.
guideDeaAudience: People building or operating ETL systems, data lakes, and analytics platforms.
guideMlaScope: Covers preparing training data, developing and deploying models, and monitoring models and infrastructure.
guideMlaWhy: Tests both machine learning evaluation metrics and deployment and operations on AWS.
guideMlaAudience: ML engineers who want to put trained models into production and continuously manage quality and cost.
guideSapScope: Covers cloud architecture across an organization, security and governance, cost, migration and business continuity, and operational automation. Architectures incorporating AI/ML are also included.
guideSapWhy: You evaluate operations, cost, and recovery requirements together when multiple accounts and existing systems impose overlapping constraints.
guideSapAudience: Architects reviewing designs across teams, and technical leads responsible for cloud migration or standardization.
guideDopScope: Covers CI/CD, configuration management, monitoring, incident response, and automating security and availability.
guideDopWhy: Requires designing end-to-end operations, from deployment across environments to rollback after anomaly detection.
guideDopAudience: DevOps engineers and SREs responsible for release platforms across teams or cloud operations automation.
guideAipScope: Covers designing generative AI applications with foundation models, RAG, agents, evaluation, safety, and production operations.
guideAipWhy: You consider retrieval and generation quality, access control, latency, and inference cost together.
guideAipAudience: Developers and architects taking generative AI features from validation to production operations.
guideScsScope: Covers identity and access management, encryption, infrastructure protection, threat detection, investigation, and incident response.
guideScsWhy: You read IAM, resource, and key policies across accounts together to determine actual permissions and denials.
guideScsAudience: People responsible for cloud security architecture, audits, or vulnerability response.
guideAnsScope: Covers AWS and on-premises connectivity, network architecture, routing, operations, and troubleshooting.
guideAnsWhy: Requires tracing BGP routes, DNS forwarding direction, and reachability across VPCs from the given conditions.
guideAnsAudience: People designing or operating hybrid infrastructure with Direct Connect or Transit Gateway.
guideAiBusinessScope: Covers prioritizing AI investments, measuring business value, managing risk, and organizational adoption and sustained use.
guideAiBusinessWhy: Beyond AI fundamentals, requires comparing business outcomes, adoption readiness, and governance case by case.
guideAiBusinessAudience: Business leaders, product leaders, and consultants responsible for AI adoption decisions.

assessmentF1Prompt: When running Linux on EC2, who is responsible for applying security patches to the guest OS?
assessmentF2Prompt: You want a discount on compute charges through a spending commitment even after moving from EC2 to Fargate. What should you consider?
assessmentA1Prompt: At peak times, requests exceed the database write capacity. You can tolerate processing delays but want to keep accepting requests. Which change is appropriate?
assessmentA1Option3: Place a queue between request intake and database writes
assessmentA2Prompt: Replication to another Region can lag by up to 5 minutes, and the switchover procedure takes 30 minutes. Which metrics describe this?
assessmentA2Option1: RPO is 5 minutes and RTO is 30 minutes
assessmentA2Option2: RPO is 30 minutes and RTO is 5 minutes
assessmentA2Option3: Both RPO and RTO are 30 minutes
assessmentS1Prompt: You read S3 data encrypted with a KMS key owned by another account through an IAM role. S3 permissions are already allowed. What must you check in KMS?
assessmentS1Option2: The key owner's key policy and the reader's IAM policy
assessmentS2Prompt: An ECS Fargate application operates on a specific SQS queue. Where should permission be granted?
assessmentN1Prompt: You want on-premises hosts connected by VPN to reach S3 without using public destination IPs. Which endpoint should you use?
assessmentN2Prompt: Between a VPC security group and network ACL, which is stateless and therefore requires return-direction rules too?
assessmentD1Prompt: Lambda receives batches from SQS. You want to avoid retrying successful records when one record fails. Which setting should you use?
assessmentD1Option1: Partial batch responses returning only failed IDs
assessmentD2Prompt: The response may be lost immediately after a payment API succeeds. How do you prevent double charges when SQS redelivers an order?
assessmentD2Option1: Use a different payment key on every attempt
assessmentD2Option2: Use a common idempotency key when retrying the same order
assessmentD2Option3: Delete the message before making the payment
assessmentO1Prompt: During an ECS rolling deployment, you want to detect startup failures and automatically return to the most recently completed deployment. What should you configure?
assessmentO2Prompt: You need to determine who called an AWS API. Which record do you normally consult?
assessmentE1Prompt: In Athena, you aggregate only some columns from daily logs. Which layout reduces scanning by both date and column?
assessmentE1Option1: Put everything in one uncompressed CSV
assessmentE1Option3: Enable versioning on the S3 bucket
assessmentE2Prompt: A new Kinesis consumer needs to reread the previous seven days. Which stream setting should you prepare?
assessmentE2Option2: Set the shard count to one
assessmentE2Option3: Set the retention period to the required duration in advance
assessmentI1Prompt: Internal documents change frequently. How can you generate answers using current document excerpts without retraining the model?
assessmentI1Option1: Retrieve documents with RAG and pass them as context
assessmentI1Option2: Fine-tune the model after every update
assessmentI2Prompt: A classification model is accurate only on data seen during validation. How do you verify generalization in the final evaluation?
assessmentI2Option1: Continue tuning hyperparameters on the same validation data
assessmentI2Option2: Evaluate on test data not used for tuning
assessmentI2Option3: Compare accuracy using only training data

subnetAddressReservationScope: This question covers VPC subnets using standard Amazon-provided IPv4 addresses and excludes BYOIP exceptions.
archivedSloCorrection: This older version has been revised. An SLO definition specifies what is measured, the success condition and denominator, the target value, and the evaluation period. Alert thresholds and notifications are separate operational settings. Past scores are unchanged.
archivedTaxTestClarification: This older version has a revision that clarifies the wording. Fix the mapping of timestamps, tax rates, and expected values, then use a fixed clock to reproduce and verify each effective date. This does not recommend changing expected values each time to match the current date.
archivedQualityGateClarification: This older version has a revision that clarifies the assumptions. For this question, treat type checking as a required gate. Stop a release if a required integration test or type check fails.
archivedFirewallScopeClarification: This archived question has been revised. The current version covers domain-based outbound traffic control and organization-wide policy application. Support for distributing TLS decryption settings through Firewall Manager was not verified for the archived version, so do not rely on it as evidence of that capability. Past scores remain unchanged.
archivedCognitoAdaptiveMfaClarification: The premise in this older version has been revised. Users who have enabled MFA receive an MFA challenge regardless of the adaptive authentication risk settings, so the former premise that routine sign-ins require no extra step does not hold. The current version concerns users who have not enabled MFA in a user pool where MFA is optional, and covers requiring MFA or blocking sign-ins according to risk. Past scoring records will remain unchanged.
archivedSnsClientErrorClarification: The premise in this older version has been revised. For client-side delivery errors, such as insufficient permissions, SNS does not retry delivery. The current version distinguishes client-side errors, which are not retried, from server-side errors, for which SNS retries delivery, and handles the body of a notification that could not be delivered to the target subscription in that subscription's DLQ. Past scoring records will remain unchanged.
archivedSqsRedriveRateClarification: The premise in this older version has been revised. The rate specified for an SQS DLQ redrive is an upper limit on the redrive rate, not a fixed throughput that is always maintained. The current version asks about setting a low upper limit for the redrive, and past scoring records will remain unchanged.
archivedDatabaseInsightsCaptureClarifica: The premise in this older version has been revised. Lock relationships from the past that were not collected cannot necessarily be reconstructed later. The current version explicitly requires enabling collection before the next incident, collecting data while it is occurring, and reviewing it after the incident. Past scoring records will remain unchanged.
archivedBackupPolicyPrerequisitesClarifi: This archived version's conditions and explanations have been revised. For AWS Backup-supported storage resources, enable the backup policy type in the organization and attach the policy. Trusted access is required for organization-wide job monitoring and is distinct from distributing plans. Historical scoring records are unchanged.
